2026-11-29.title: Sunday of the Visitation of Mary, Mother of God, to Elizabeth
readings: The deaf shall hear, the blind shall see
God desires everyone to be saved
2026-11-29.alt: Third Sunday of Suboro. The Twenty-Five Days Nombu (fast before Yaldo) begins on Tuesday 1 December.
2026-11-29.verse: And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
theo: After the angel leaves, Mary does not stay at home to enjoy her secret. St Luke says she “set out and went with haste” to the hill country to visit Elizabeth. The first thing the Mother of God does, with the Son of God in her womb, is to serve. Faith that has received Christ goes out.

When Mary greets Elizabeth, the child John leaps in his mother's womb and Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit. John, who will later point to the Lamb of God, recognises him already before birth. Elizabeth cries out: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb… why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?” With these words the Church has greeted Mary ever since.

Mary answers with the Magnificat: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.” Her song is full of the Old Testament, especially Hannah's song: “My heart exults in the LORD… He raises up the poor from the dust” (1 Samuel 2:1, 8). God looks on the lowly, scatters the proud, fills the hungry, and remembers his mercy to Abraham. Mary sings not about herself but about God.

The readings also praise faithful women: Rebekah's kindness at the well (Genesis 24), the capable wife of Proverbs 31, whose strength is the fear of the Lord. Mary is blessed above all because she believed. And St Paul reminds us that God “desires everyone to be saved” (1 Timothy 2:4). The Visitation is the first Christian mission: Christ carried to a home, and a home filled with joy.
conn: The Ark comes to the hill country.

David asked, “How can the ark of the LORD come into my care?” and the ark stayed three months in the house of Obed-edom (2 Samuel 6:9–11). Elizabeth asks, “Why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?” and Mary stays about three months (Luke 1:56). Mary is the new Ark.
Both sing after God has worked a wonder in a woman's womb; both praise the God who lifts up the lowly.
Rebekah's prompt, generous service to a stranger (Genesis 24:18–20) foreshadows Mary hurrying to serve Elizabeth.
The deaf hear, the blind see.
Isaiah 29:18 is fulfilled when the unborn John “hears” Mary's greeting and leaps for joy.
altar: Mary carried Christ hidden within her into Elizabeth's house. After every Holy Qurbono we too go home carrying Christ within us. The Visitation teaches us what to do after Communion: go in haste to serve, and bring joy.
outline: Ask: what is the first thing you do after receiving good news?
Mary “went with haste” to serve. Receiving Christ leads to mission.
John recognises Christ before birth: a word on the dignity of the unborn.
God lifts the lowly and fills the hungry. Mary's song is a programme of Christian life.
The 25-day Nombu begins: prayer, fasting and visiting someone who needs us.
“Blessed is she who believed.” Blessed are we when we believe.
live: During the Nombu, visit an elderly, sick or lonely person in your family or parish.
Pray Mary's song each evening this week, slowly, thanking God for one gift of the day.
Decide now how your family will keep the fast from 1 December: food, screens, and charity.
fathers: “Let the soul of Mary be in each one of you to magnify the Lord; let the spirit of Mary be in each one to rejoice in God” (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke 2, 26).
He calls the Magnificat a song to be sung daily by the Church, because it teaches us to give glory to God for the gift of the Incarnation (Homilies on the Gospels I, 4).
magis: In the Visitation Mary is blessed for her faith; Elizabeth's words reveal the “obedience of faith” by which Mary welcomed the Word.
Mary is the woman who “sets out in haste”; there is a Marian “style” in the Church's evangelising work: tenderness, humility and service.
The words of Elizabeth, together with the angel's greeting, form the first part of the Hail Mary.
saints: 30 Nov: St Andrew, Apostle. 1 Dec: beginning of the Twenty-Five Days Nombu. 3 Dec: St Francis Xavier. 4 Dec: St John Damascene. Confirm in the 2026–27 lectionary.
2026-11-29.prayer: Lord God, Mary carried your Son in haste to Elizabeth and filled her house with joy. As we begin the fast before Yaldo, make us carry Christ to those who need him, and let our souls, with hers, magnify your name. Amen.

quick: Mary, carrying Christ, goes in haste to serve.
John leaps for joy: Christ is recognised even before birth.
The Magnificat: God lifts the lowly and fills the hungry.
2026-11-29.action: During the Nombu, visit someone who is lonely or sick.
2026-11-29.question: Whom is God asking me to visit this Nombu?
2026-11-29.special: Third Sunday of Suboro. Remind the faithful that the Twenty-Five Days Nombu begins on 1 December.
illus: In many Kerala parishes the family units visit the homes of the sick before Christmas with a carol and a small gift. The visit costs little, but people remember it for years. That is the Visitation in our own day.

family.explain: When Mary heard that her cousin Elizabeth was expecting a baby, she hurried to help her. Baby John jumped for joy because Jesus had come close!
family.intention: We pray for mothers who are expecting a baby, and for all the unborn children.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can our family visit or help before Christmas?”

catechism: John the Baptist, filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother's womb.
The Magnificat, the song of the Mother of God and of the Church.
kidsaint: A fisherman who met Jesus and ran to tell his brother Simon: “We have found the Messiah!” He brought Peter to Jesus. Lesson: when you find something good, share it, especially Jesus.
term: The fast before Yaldo (Christmas), kept from 1 to 25 December. It is a time of prayer, abstinence and charity, preparing to welcome Christ.
termMore: Mary's song (Luke 1:46–55), named after its first word in Latin. It is sung daily in the evening prayer of the Church in many traditions.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, what do we do when we receive great news? We pick up the phone and tell someone. When Mary received the greatest news in history, she did something more: she set out and went with haste to the hill country, to help her elderly cousin Elizabeth.

Imagine the scene. Mary greets Elizabeth, and the baby in Elizabeth's womb leaps for joy. John recognises Jesus before either of them is born. Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, says: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.” Every time we pray the Hail Mary, we repeat her words.

Then Mary sings: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.” She does not sing about herself. She sings about a God who looks on the lowly, lifts up the poor, fills the hungry with good things, and sends the proud away empty. Like Hannah before her, she knows that God works through the small and the humble.

On Tuesday the Twenty-Five Days Nombu begins. Let us keep it like Mary: not only by giving up food, but by going out. Visit someone who is old, sick or lonely. Carry Christ to them, as Mary did. And after every Holy Qurbono, remember: you leave this church as Mary left Nazareth, carrying the Lord within you. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary had a cousin called Elizabeth who was going to have a baby. Mary walked a long way over the hills to help her.
When Mary said hello, baby John jumped inside Elizabeth's tummy, because Jesus was there inside Mary! John was so happy.
Before Christmas, let's be like Mary: help someone at home, visit Grandma or Grandpa, and bring Jesus' joy. Let's say: “I will bring Jesus to others!”

intro: Mary has just said “yes” to God. Her first act is not to stay home in wonder but to set out in haste to help her elderly cousin. Where Mary goes, Christ goes, and the Spirit fills a home with joy.

sub: She goes “with haste” to the hill country: love does not delay.
At her greeting the child leaps in Elizabeth's womb, and Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit.
Like Abraham's servant led by God to Rebekah's house, Mary is led to the home that needs her.
q: Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his steadfast love and his faithfulness toward my master.

When Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the child leaped in her womb. And Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit and exclaimed with a loud cry, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.”
points.apply: Visit someone who is old, sick or alone this week, and take Christ with you in your kindness.

sub: Elizabeth praises Mary first for her faith, not her privilege.
True beauty, says Proverbs, is the fear of the Lord.
Our families are blessed not by wealth or appearance but by faith lived together.
q: Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
points.apply: Thank God for a woman of faith who formed you: mother, grandmother, teacher, sister.

points.h: The Magnificat: God lifts up the lowly
sub: Mary sings like Hannah before her: joy in God the Saviour.
God looks at the lowly; he scatters the proud and fills the hungry.
Mary's song is the song of the poor Church, and a call to serve the poor.
q: He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap.
My spirit rejoices in God my Savior, for he has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant.
points.apply: Pray the Magnificat each evening this week.

concl: The Visitation shows the Church's mission: to carry Christ to every home, to serve with haste, and to sing God's praise.
May our visits, words and works make others' hearts leap with joy.
2026-11-29.resolve: Make one visit of charity this week, and pray the Magnificat with your family.
